known_final_diagnosis: The diagnosis of GPA was based on the presence of suggestive clinical signs, notably the notion of hemoptysis, anemia, and suggestive appearance in the scan: multifocal ground glass with respect for the periphery, association of septal lines (crazy paving), and the presence of siderophages in the BAL. The diagnosis was also based on the American College of Rheumatology (ACR)/European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) 2022 classification criteria: the presence of c-ANCA and chest X-ray abnormalities (5 points) (Figure 3).

report.source_text: The patient received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone corticosteroids (1,000 mg/day) for three consecutive days. Treatment was subsequently changed to oral prednisone (1 mg/kg), with progressive dose reduction until a dose of 10 mg/d was maintained. After high-dose treatment, asthenia and cough disappeared, with improvement in his oxygen saturation. After the definitive diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis, corticosteroids were eliminated, and treatment continued.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old female presented with diffuse interstitial lung disease, chronic anemia, low-grade hemoptysis, and exposure to poultry and essential oils. Chest CT showed diffuse bilateral ground glass opacities with septal and non-septal thickening giving a crazy paving pattern suggestive of alveolar hemorrhage. Immunological workup revealed positive c-ANCA with cytoplasmic fluorescence and negative p-ANCA, supportive of GPA. Bronchoscopy with BAL demonstrated histiocytic macrophagic alveolitis with hemosiderosis indicating alveolar hemorrhage. The diagnosis was confirmed using the ACR/EULAR 2022 classification criteria based on c-ANCA positivity and chest X-ray abnormalities. The patient was treated with high-dose intravenous then oral corticosteroids, resulting in symptomatic and oxygenation improvement.

Immunological workup revealed c-ANCA positivity with cytoplasmic fluorescence, p-ANCA negative, strongly suggesting GPA.
Bronchoscopy with BAL and Perls' staining showed macrophagic alveolitis with hemosiderosis indicating alveolar hemorrhage.
Diagnosis based on ACR/EULAR 2022 classification criteria: presence of c-ANCA and chest X-ray abnormalities scoring 5 points confirms GPA.
Patient treated with high-dose corticosteroids with subsequent clinical and oxygenation improvement.
